chunk_findings.detail: The new landed-change guard only fails closed when `HEAD` is exactly the base branch head. If the item has already been merged but is being evaluated from a worktree whose `HEAD` is still the merged item commit (an ancestor of `base`), the equality test is false and the guard does not fire. Example: item branch commit `A` adds logic; after landing, `base` is `A` plus a docs-only commit `D` outside the item's logic paths. Calling this function from the item worktree with `item.base = base` sees `head.out != basecommit.out`, continues to `_is_format_or_comment(tree, base, paths)`, and that comparison over the item's paths sees no AST change, so it can return True. The already-landed logic change is then still classified trivial, defeating the stated fix. The check should fail closed when the item's committed change is already contained in `base` (e.g. ancestor/empty `base...HEAD`), not only when the two SHAs are equal.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docsonly.py:89

chunk_findings.detail: The new holder-consent bypass trusts the caller-supplied `queued_by` string without proving that the call is the queue integrator or that a matching queue entry exists. Given an item with a live lease held by agent `A`, another agent `B` can call `merge(..., agent="B", queued_by="A")`; `LS.peer_live_lease` returns `A`'s lease, `_queued_by_holder` returns true, and the lease-refusal branch is skipped, letting `B` land `A`'s branch and end `A`'s lease.

chunk_findings.detail: In `_setup`, `_git(repo, "add", "-A")` and `_git(repo, "commit", "-qm", "task")` are executed on `repo` while it is still on the initial `main` branch before checking out `feat`, but the task add command `run_cli(repo, "task", "add", "T1", ...)` is executed immediately before these commits. In ddflow, item and task state files (such as under `.ddflow/`) must be committed or handled correctly, but committing them on `main` immediately after creating a task while `repo` is about to switch to `feat` breaks the intended repository state setup for branch `feat` reviewed heads, causing tests like `test_a_commit_made_while_a_full_review_runs_shows_up_in_the_next_delta` to fail because the task record is not part of the `feat` branch commit history where work is added (`_git(repo, "checkout", "-q", "-b", "feat")` happens *after* the task commit).

chunk_findings.detail: `queued_by` is an unchecked caller argument, so the peer-lease refusal is bypassed whenever it equals `held.holder`. A same-clone agent calls `land(..., agent=<peer>, queued_by=<live lease holder>)` — the holder id is on the lease — and the `if held is not None and not _queued_by_holder(...)` guard falls through, landing another agent’s leased item. Nothing checks that the caller is the merge-queue integrator or that a queue entry actually exists; `mergequeue_run` passing `e.agent` does not constrain other callers of `land`.

chunk_findings.detail: `git -C <late-wt> rev-parse --git-path index.lock` prints a path relative to the process cwd (or absolute), not a path relative to the worktree. Five tests (review_head_at_diff x4, review_snapshot_at_start) had to be rebuilt to commit outside the watched tree or stub the guard.

chunk_findings.detail: The new consent check still lets any same-clone agent land an item whose lease is held by the agent that merely queued it. Suppose agent A holds a live lease on item I and has queued I, so the queue entry is RUNNING with `entry.agent == A`. While the real integrator has marked the entry RUNNING but before it calls `land`, another agent B calls `land(repo, I, agent=B, ...)`. `LS.peer_live_lease` returns A's live lease because B is a peer, but `_queued_by_holder` returns True solely from `MQ.get(repo, I).state == RUNNING` and `entry.agent == A`; it never checks that B is the merge-queue integrator or the agent recorded as running the queue entry. Thus B lands I and ends A's lease, preserving the consent bypass the queue-entry fix was meant to close.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/merge.py:_queued_by_holder

chunk_findings.detail: The confirmed bypass is only half closed. `_queued_by_holder` treats any `MQ.RUNNING` entry whose `agent` equals `held.holder` as consent, and the guard at the `land` peer-lease check never compares that entry to the caller (`agent` / `log.agent_id`). While the integrator has the entry in `RUNNING` (the window in which `mergequeue_run` calls `land`), a same-clone peer `P` can call `land(repo, item, agent=P)`. `ID.is_agent(P)` is true, `peer_live_lease` still returns holder `H`'s live lease, and the new predicate returns true because `entry.agent == H`, so the refusal is skipped and `P` lands `H`'s leased item. Consent is no longer a free argument, but it is still not bound to the integrator that is actually running the queue entry.

While the real integrator has marked the entry RUNNING but before it calls `land`, another agent B calls `land(repo, I, agent=B, ...)`. `LS.peer_live_lease` returns A's live lease because B is a peer, but `_queued_by_holder` returns True solely from `MQ.get(repo, I).state == RUNNING` and `entry.agent == A`; it never checks that B is the merge-queue integrator or the agent recorded as running the queue entry. Thus B lands I and ends A's lease, preserving the consent bypass the queue-entry fix was meant to close.

chunk_findings.detail: The confirmed bypass is only half closed. `_queued_by_holder` treats any `MQ.RUNNING` entry whose `agent` equals `held.holder` as consent, and the guard at the `land` peer-lease check never compares that entry to the caller (`agent` / `log.agent_id`). While the integrator has the entry in `RUNNING` (the window in which `mergequeue_run` calls `land`), a same-clone peer `P` can call `land(repo, item, agent=P)`. `ID.is_agent(P)` is true, `peer_live_lease` still returns holder `H`'s live lease, and the new predicate returns true because `entry.agent == H`, so the refusal is skipped and `P` lands `H`'s leased item. Consent is no longer a free argument, but it is still not bound to the integrator that is actually running the queue entry.
